title: A Unified Online-Offline Framework for Co-Branding Campaign Recommendations

problem.claim: Recommendation systems need to identify effective cross-industry co-branding partnerships to expand market reach.

gap.claim: Effective partnership identification is difficult because of resource imbalances, uncertain brand willingness, and changing market conditions.

contributions.claim: A unified online-offline framework enables co-branding recommendations.
The framework uses a bipartite initiating-brand/target-brand graph, dynamically updates it from market feedback, and balances exploration with exploitation.
The paper provides a sublinear regret bound for online learning and improves the approximation guarantee for the NP-hard offline budget allocation problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world co-branding datasets reportedly show at least 12% improvement.
The framework reportedly mitigates redundant exploration to improve short-term performance while supporting sustainable strategic growth.
Offline optimization reportedly consolidates multiple sub-brand interests under a parent brand to maximize overall returns and reduce unnecessary costs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Co-branding is presented as a strategy for expanding market reach in recommendation systems.
Cross-industry partnership identification is challenged by imbalances, uncertain willingness, and market change.
The paper proposes a unified online-offline framework based on a bipartite brand graph and adaptive exploration-exploitation.
The framework reduces redundant exploration online and consolidates parent-brand sub-brand interests during offline budget allocation.
The paper reports theoretical guarantees and at least 12% improvement in synthetic and real-world experiments.

unknowns: Specific dataset sizes, baselines, metrics, and experimental settings are not provided.
The assumptions and exact form of the regret bound and approximation guarantee are not provided.
The meaning and statistical basis of the reported 12% improvement are not specified.
